question.text: A protection strategy against longevity risk includes:

answer.text: Investing only in short-term deposits that mature every year
Purchasing a deferred annuity that begins paying income in mid-to-late retirement
Keeping all retirement savings in cash
Withdrawing the entire NPS corpus as lump sum

explanation.text: The Logic: Buying a deferred annuity that locks in lifetime income starting later in retirement is a recognised way to manage longevity risk, as per the workbook. The Trap: Short-term deposits do not provide lifetime income. A lump-sum NPS withdrawal removes the longevity protection embedded in the scheme's mandatory annuitization. Note: NPS mandates a minimum 40 percent annuitization at exit, which itself addresses longevity risk for retirees.
